items.title: Grammar 1–3

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Introduce Someone with 叫, 姓, and 是
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Introduce someone by name, surname, or identity.
grammarPages.explanation: 叫, 姓 and 是 are used as verbs and equate two nouns in a sentence. 姓 comes only before a family name. 叫 comes before a given name or a full name. 是 says what someone is. Put 不 before them to say no.
grammarPages.pattern: Subject +（Neg）叫／姓／是 + Noun

patternRows.english: His name is Zhongming.
Whose surname is Li?
He is not Taiwanese.

text.traditional: A：她是誰？ B：她是新同學。
text.simplified: A：她是谁？ B：她是新同学。
text.pinyin: A: Tā shì shéi? B: Tā shì xīn tóngxué.
text.english: A: Who is she? B: She is a new classmate.

text.traditional: 她是日本人，她不是台灣人。
text.simplified: 她是日本人，她不是台湾人。
text.pinyin: Tā shì Rìběn rén, tā bú shì Táiwān rén.
text.english: She is Japanese. She is not Taiwanese.

text.traditional: 她不姓李，她姓小林，叫小林友美。
text.simplified: 她不姓李，她姓小林，叫小林友美。
text.pinyin: Tā bú xìng Lǐ, tā xìng Xiǎolín, jiào Xiǎolín Yǒuměi.
text.english: Her surname is not Li. Her surname is Xiaolin; her name is Xiaolin Youmei.

items.question: Does 姓 take the full name too?
items.answer: 姓 takes only a family name; use 叫 before a given name or full name.

right.traditional: 她不姓李，她姓小林，叫小林友美。
right.simplified: 她不姓李，她姓小林，叫小林友美。
right.pinyin: Tā bú xìng Lǐ, tā xìng Xiǎolín, jiào Xiǎolín Yǒuměi.
right.english: Her surname is not Li. Her surname is Xiaolin; her name is Xiaolin Youmei.

items.question: Can 姓 introduce a given name?
items.answer: Use 叫 before the given name 中明; 姓 takes only a family name.

right.english: His name is Zhongming.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Describe Someone with 很 or 不
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say that someone is or is not busy, tired, or pretty.
grammarPages.explanation: Put 很 or 不 before adjectives like 漂亮, 可愛, 忙 and 累. These words already carry the meaning of "is", so no 是 is needed. 很 can mean "very"; 不 means "not".
grammarPages.pattern: Subject + 很／不 + Adjective

columns.meaning: very; the usual word before a description

text.simplified: 她很可爱。
text.pinyin: Tā hěn kě'ài.
text.english: She is cute.

text.simplified: 我们不累，王太太很累。
text.pinyin: Wǒmen bú lèi, Wáng tàitai hěn lèi.
text.english: We are not tired; Mrs. Wang is very tired.

words.meaning: very; the usual word before a description

items.question: English says "she IS pretty" — where is 是?
items.answer: Nowhere. Words like 漂亮 already carry the meaning of "is", so use 很 or 不, not 是.

items.answer: Put 不 before the word: 不累. 是 has no job in this pattern.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Ask a Yes/No Question with 嗎
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Turn a statement into a yes-or-no question with one ending word.
grammarPages.explanation: Add 嗎 at the very end of the statement, without any change in order. Nothing inside the sentence moves. The listener answers yes or no.
grammarPages.pattern: Statement + 嗎

patternRows.english: Is he Taiwanese?
Is she pretty?

text.traditional: A：他是日本人嗎？ B：他不是日本人，他是台灣人。
text.simplified: A：他是日本人吗？ B：他不是日本人，他是台湾人。
text.pinyin: A: Tā shì Rìběn rén ma? B: Tā bú shì Rìběn rén, tā shì Táiwān rén.
text.english: A: Is he Japanese? B: He is not Japanese; he is Taiwanese.

text.traditional: 高先生叫家樂嗎？
text.simplified: 高先生叫家乐吗？
text.pinyin: Gāo xiānsheng jiào Jiālè ma?
text.english: Is Mr. Gao called Jiale?

text.traditional: 他忙嗎？
text.simplified: 他忙吗？
text.pinyin: Tā máng ma?
text.english: Is he busy?

items.question: Where does 嗎 go?
items.answer: At the very end. The whole statement stays first, exactly in its order.

right.english: Is he Japanese?

items.question: Do I keep 嗎 when I answer?
items.answer: No. 嗎 only asks a question; the answer is the plain statement.

right.traditional: 他不是日本人，他是台灣人。
right.simplified: 他不是日本人，他是台湾人。
right.pinyin: Tā bú shì Rìběn rén, tā shì Táiwān rén.
right.english: He is not Japanese; he is Taiwanese.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Use 呢 to Say “And You?”
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Ask the same question back with 呢, without repeating the whole sentence.
grammarPages.explanation: When a question is already in the air, say the new person or thing, add 呢, and stop. 呢 repeats that question for the new person without saying the sentence again.
grammarPages.pattern: Statement, + new topic + 呢

patternRows.english: I am Taiwanese. How about you?
Yiwen's surname is Wang. How about Zhongming?

text.traditional: A：我是日本人，你呢？ B：我是臺灣人。
text.simplified: A：我是日本人，你呢？ B：我是台湾人。
text.pinyin: A: Wǒ shì Rìběn rén, nǐ ne? B: Wǒ shì Táiwān rén.
text.english: A: I am Japanese. How about you? B: I am Taiwanese.

text.traditional: A：小林小姐叫友美，李先生呢？ B：他叫中明。
text.simplified: A：小林小姐叫友美，李先生呢？ B：他叫中明。
text.pinyin: A: Xiǎolín xiǎojiě jiào Yǒuměi, Lǐ xiānsheng ne? B: Tā jiào Zhōngmíng.
text.english: A: Miss Xiaolin is called Youmei. How about Mr. Li? B: He is called Zhongming.

text.pinyin: A: Wáng tàitai hěn lèi, Wáng xiānsheng ne? B: Tā bú lèi.
text.english: A: Mrs. Wang is very tired. How about Mr. Wang? B: He is not tired.

grammarPages.titleTraditional: 主語 + 動詞 + 受詞
grammarPages.titleEnglish: Subject–Verb–Object Structure
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Build a complete sentence with a subject, a verb, and an object, in that order.
grammarPages.explanation: The book's pattern keeps one order: subject, then verb, then object. The object is the person or thing the verb affects. Put 不 right before the verb to say the opposite.
grammarPages.pattern: S + (Neg)V + O

patternRows.english: I (don't) like him.

text.traditional: 我喜歡李小姐，不喜歡王小姐。
text.simplified: 我喜欢李小姐，不喜欢王小姐。
text.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuān Lǐ xiǎojiě, bù xǐhuān Wáng xiǎojiě.
text.english: I like Miss Li, but I do not like Miss Wang.

examples.teachingNote: The second part does not repeat 我.

text.traditional: 你喜歡什麼？
text.simplified: 你喜欢什么？
text.pinyin: Nǐ xǐhuān shénme?
text.english: What do you like?

examples.teachingNote: 什麼 takes the object's place when you ask what someone likes.

text.traditional: 我愛爸爸、媽媽。
text.simplified: 我爱爸爸、妈妈。
text.pinyin: Wǒ ài bàba, māma.
text.english: I love Dad and Mom.

examples.teachingNote: One verb can take two objects.

items.question: Does 愛 need 是 before its object?
items.answer: Put 爸爸、媽媽 directly after 愛 without 是.

right.english: I love Dad and Mom.

items.question: Where does 不 go?
items.answer: Right before the verb, in the (Neg) V slot.

grammarPages.titleTraditional: 這／那／哪 + 數字 + 量詞 + 名詞
grammarPages.titleEnglish: Point to This, That, or Which Thing
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Point to things that are near or far, or ask which one someone means.
grammarPages.explanation: Start with 這, 那, or 哪, then add the number, measure word, and noun. With one item, 一 is often omitted; with two, use 兩. 這, 那, and 哪 mean “this,” “that,” and “which.” Use 這 when the noun is close and 那 when it is far.

ending word for a yes-or-no question
how is it; what do you think
two; plain-count form (two becomes 兩 before a measure word)
one; usually omitted between 這/那/哪 and the measure word

grammarPages.pattern: 這 / 那 / 哪 + number + measure word + noun

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Describe a Noun or Replace It with 的
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Describe the thing you want and avoid repeating an obvious noun.
grammarPages.explanation: Use 的 to link a describing word to a noun. With short one-syllable words, you can usually skip 的. If the topic is already clear, drop the noun and keep just 的.

teachingGlossary.meaning: connects a describing word to a thing; can stand for a known thing
ending word for a yes-or-no question
how is it; what do you think
的 when it is dropped with one-syllable words
cake, already mentioned so it is omitted

grammarPages.pattern: Description + 的 + noun, or description + 的

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Express a Learned Ability with 會
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say what someone knows—or does not know—how to do.
grammarPages.explanation: 會 marks a skill you get through learning. Put it before the action: 我會游泳. Negate with 不會: 我不會打棒球.

teachingGlossary.meaning: shows belonging or links a describing word

grammarPages.pattern: Subject +（Neg）會 + verb

discoveryLab.title: Flip the skill switch

choices.note: 不 goes directly before 會.

choices.label: Ask about a skill

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Describe How Well You Do an Action with 得
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Describe how well, fast, slowly, much, or happily an action is done.
grammarPages.explanation: Use 得 after a verb to describe how well you do it: 跑得很快. If there is an object, repeat the verb (跑步跑得很快) or say the object first (網球打得很好).

teachingGlossary.meaning: shows how an action is done
shows belonging or links a describing word

grammarPages.pattern: Subject + Verb + 得 + Adjective

discoveryLab.title: Choose the lane to 得
discoveryLab.description: Every lane ends with verb + 得 + performance. The activity’s shape decides what comes before it.

choices.label: Simple verb
choices.pinyin: Tā pǎo de hěn kuài.
choices.english: He runs very fast.
choices.note: The action word 跑 goes straight before 得.

choices.label: Repeat the verb
choices.pinyin: Wǒ pǎobù pǎo de hěn kuài.
choices.english: I run very fast.
choices.note: Say the full activity 跑步, then repeat the action word 跑 before 得.

choices.label: Move object forward
choices.pinyin: Tā wǎngqiú dǎ de búcuò.
choices.english: He plays tennis quite well.
choices.note: 網球 becomes the topic, leaving 打 next to 得.

choices.label: Owned activity
choices.traditional: 他的牛肉麵做得很不錯。
choices.simplified: 他的牛肉面做得很不错。
choices.pinyin: Tā de niúròumiàn zuò de hěn búcuò.
choices.english: He cooks good beef noodles.
choices.note: 他的牛肉麵 is the topic; 做 still stands directly before 得.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Protect the core: action word + 得 + performance. Move or repeat the thing when needed.

sentenceSpine.title: Build the unbreakable core
sentenceSpine.description: Three blocks. The middle block is the rule that never changes.
notes: Right: 跑步 + 跑得 + 很快. Repeat 跑 so the action word touches 得.
Wrong: 跑步 + 得 + 很快. The word 步 cannot attach directly to 得.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Say “A Little” with 有一點兒
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Describe a small, often inconvenient degree: a little tired, cold, or small.
grammarPages.explanation: Use 有一點兒 (or 有點兒) before a describing word to say it is slightly so — usually for a small problem.

teachingGlossary.meaning: shows belonging or links a describing word

grammarPages.pattern: Subject + 有（一）點（兒） + adjective

discoveryLab.title: Turn up only one notch
discoveryLab.description: The dial makes the describing word softer — often before you explain a problem or say no.

choices.note: The clothes look nice, but they are a little small.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Say who or what first, then 有點兒, then the describing word. One small notch, often for a mild problem.

contrast.title: A little vs. a little amount

items.note: 點兒 measures a small amount of 飲料.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Ask and Give Permission with 可以
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Offer a possible solution or ask whether an action is permitted.
grammarPages.explanation: Use 可以 to ask for permission or suggest a solution. Ask with 可以…嗎 or 可不可以. Answer with 可以 to allow it, or 不可以 to say no.

teachingGlossary.meaning: may or may not; can or cannot
shows belonging or links a describing word

grammarPages.pattern: Subject + 可以 + Verb; Subject + 可以 + Verb 嗎？

discoveryLab.title: Read the green-light card
discoveryLab.description: The same 可以 either opens a possible path or checks permission.
discoveryLab.prompt: What job is 可以 doing?

choices.label: Suggestion
choices.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ diǎn yì bēi rè chá.
choices.english: You could order a cup of hot tea.
choices.note: A problem comes first; 可以 offers one useful option.

choices.label: Ask permission
choices.traditional: 老師，我現在可以去洗手間嗎？
choices.simplified: 老师，我现在可以去洗手间吗？
choices.pinyin: Lǎoshī, wǒ xiànzài kěyǐ qù xǐshǒujiān ma?
choices.english: Teacher, may I go to the restroom now?
choices.note: The speaker asks whether the action has a green light.

choices.label: No permission
choices.traditional: 不可以，也不可以喝飲料。
choices.simplified: 不可以，也不可以喝饮料。
choices.pinyin: Bù kěyǐ, yě bù kěyǐ hē yǐnliào.
choices.english: No. Drinking is not allowed either.
choices.note: 不可以 removes permission.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Problem + 可以 = possible solution. 可以…嗎 = permission check.

contrast.title: Learned ability or permission
contrast.description: Both can translate as “can,” but they answer different questions.

items.label: Permission
items.note: 可以 asks whether the action is allowed.

items.question: May I go to the restroom? Is it 我去可以洗手間嗎?
items.answer: Put 可以 before the verb 去.

right.traditional: 老師，我現在可以去洗手間嗎？
right.simplified: 老师，我现在可以去洗手间吗？
right.pinyin: Lǎoshī, wǒ xiànzài kěyǐ qù xǐshǒujiān ma?
right.english: Teacher, may I go to the restroom now?

items.question: To ask Mom if I may have ice cream, can I say 我想吃冰淇淋嗎?
items.answer: No — 想 means want. To ask permission, use 可以: 我可以吃冰淇淋嗎？

right.english: May I eat ice cream?

items.question: Do I add 嗎 after 可不可以, like 可以不可以去嗎?
items.answer: No — 可不可以 is already a question. Adding 嗎 doubles the question ending.

right.simplified: 我们可不可以在捷运上吃东西？
right.pinyin: Wǒmen kě bù kěyǐ zài jiéyùn shàng chī dōngxi?

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: How Do We Get to the Hotel?
grammarPages.titleEnglish: 從 and 到: From and To
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say where someone comes from and where they go.
grammarPages.explanation: 從 means from. 到 means to. Put the place right after it, then end with 來 (come) or 去 (go).
grammarPages.pattern: Subject + 從 / 到 + place + 來 / 去

items.question: Which place follows 從?
items.answer: Put the starting place after 從 and the destination after 到.
items.wrongTraditional: 我到學校從我家去上課。

right.traditional: 我從我家到學校去上課。
right.pinyin: Wǒ cóng wǒ jiā dào xuéxiào qù shàngkè.
right.english: I go to school from my home for class.
right.simplified: 我从我家到学校走上课。

items.question: He is coming to my home; 來 or 去?
items.answer: Use 來 because the trip ends at the speaker’s home.
items.wrongTraditional: 他從旅館到我家去吃飯。

right.traditional: 他從旅館到我家來吃飯。
right.simplified: 他从旅馆到我家来吃饭。
right.pinyin: Tā cóng lǚguǎn dào wǒ jiā lái chīfàn.
right.english: He is coming from the hotel to my home to eat.

items.question: Where does 去 go in 到他家去?
items.answer: Put 去 after 到 and the destination: 到他家去.

right.english: I went to his place.

items.answer: Use 走路 for walking, without 坐.

items.question: Does the travel method go before 去?
items.answer: Put 坐公車 before 去 when it answers how you travel.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: 好 / 難 + Verb

text.english: Yuanzhen, your skirt is very beautiful; I like it very much.

text.english: Thanks, this is my birthday gift from last year.

text.pinyin: Tīngshuō zhè ge páizi de dōngxi hěn guì, kěshì hěn duō rén xǐhuān.
text.english: I heard that this clothing brand is very expensive, but a lot of people like it.

words.meaning: linking word; can stand for the noun

text.traditional: 是啊，因為這個牌子很有名，衣服、褲子和裙子也都很好看，所以很多人買。

text.pinyin: Shì a, yīnwèi zhè ge páizi hěn yǒumíng, yīfu, kùzi hé qúnzi yě dōu hěn hǎokàn, suǒyǐ hěn duō rén mǎi.
text.english: Yes, it is. This brand is very famous and its tops, pants and skirts are very beautiful, so many people buy it.

text.traditional: 妳知道去哪裡買這個牌子的衣服嗎？
text.simplified: 你知道去哪里买这个牌子的衣服吗？

text.english: Do you know where you can get this clothing brand?

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Check a Guess
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Ask someone to confirm what you think.
grammarPages.explanation: Put 吧 after a statement when you think it is true and want confirmation.

patternRows.english: You want to buy shoes, don’t you?

text.traditional: A：你會唱中文歌吧？ B：會。可是不多，我只會唱三首。
text.simplified: A：你会唱中文歌吧？ B：会。可是不多，我只会唱三首。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ huì chàng Zhōngwén gē ba? B: Huì. Kěshì bù duō, wǒ zhǐ huì chàng sān shǒu.

text.simplified: A：他平常都坐捷运来上课吧？ B：不是，他都坐公车来上课。

text.english: A: He usually comes to class by MRT, right? B: No, he always comes to class by bus.

text.english: A: You’re free now, right? Would you like to watch a tennis match with me? B: I’m free, but I want to eat something first.

items.question: Where does 吧 go?
items.answer: Put 吧 after the statement you want confirmed.

text.english: A: I hear the coffee here tastes good. B: OK, I’ll try some and see.

grammarPages.pattern: 從 + start time + 到 + finish time

patternRows.english: from 4:00 to 5:30
from Monday to Friday

items.question: Which time goes right after 從 — the start time or the finish time?
items.answer: The start time. 從 opens the start, and 到 opens the finish: 我從四點到五點半上英文課.

right.traditional: 我從四點到五點半上英文課。
right.simplified: 我从四点到五点半上英文课。
right.pinyin: Wǒ cóng sì diǎn dào wǔ diǎn bàn shàng Yīngwén kè.
right.english: I have English class from 4:00 to 5:30.

items.question: My class runs Monday to Friday. Do I need 從 — is 我星期一到星期五都有課 okay?
items.answer: Use both pins. 從 opens the start, and 到 opens the finish: 我從星期一到星期五都有課.

right.traditional: 我從星期一到星期五都有課。
right.simplified: 我从星期一到星期五都有课。
right.pinyin: Wǒ cóng xīngqí yī dào xīngqí wǔ dōu yǒu kè.
right.english: I have class from Monday to Friday.

items.question: I am busy from morning to night. Is 都 needed, and where does it go?
items.answer: Yes — 都 shows the whole range is covered. It goes right after the range: 我從早到晚都忙。

right.pinyin: Wǒ cóng zǎo dào wǎn dōu máng.
right.english: I am busy from morning to night.

grammarPages.pattern: Person + 先 + action 1，再 + action 2

patternRows.english: He plays tennis first, then swims.
My older sister sings first, then my younger sister sings.
First return to the dorm, then go find him.

items.question: Where does 先 go — before the first action or after it?
items.answer: Before it. 先 + first action, 再 + next action: 我先看書，再做功課.

right.pinyin: Wǒ xiān kànshū, zài zuò gōngkè.
right.english: I read first, then do homework.

items.question: I do both actions myself. Do I say 我 twice — 我做功課，我再去?
items.answer: No — one person doing both actions is named once: 我先做功課，再去。

right.pinyin: Wǒ xiān zuò gōngkè, zài qù.
right.english: First I do homework, then I go.

items.question: Second step: do I repeat the action word — 再坐公車 or 再公車?
items.answer: Repeat it. Each step keeps its own action word: 你要先坐捷運，再坐公車.

right.traditional: 你要先坐捷運，再坐公車。
right.simplified: 你要先坐捷运，再坐公车。

right.english: First take the MRT, then take a bus.

items.question: A friend asks 我能在這裡用電腦嗎？ Do I answer with 可以 or 能?
items.answer: 可以. Giving or asking permission uses 可以: 可以，沒問題。 能 is for ability, rules, or the situation.

right.english: Sure, no problem.

items.question: He hurt his leg and can only walk. Is it 能只走 or 只能走?
items.answer: 只能走. 只 comes before 能: 只能 + action means "can only do this one thing."

right.english: He can only walk now.

items.question: Phones are not allowed in class. Can I say 沒能看手機 for the rule?
items.answer: No. 沒能 means you did not get a chance. A rule uses 不能 or 不可以 — for permission, 能 can be replaced with 可以, and permission questions and negatives often use 可以.

right.traditional: 上課時間我們不能看手機。
right.simplified: 上课时间我们不能看手机。

right.english: We cannot look at our phones during class.

items.question: To ask "Can I use that classroom?", do I say 我能不能用那間教室嗎 with 嗎?
items.answer: No — 能不能 already asks the question, so 嗎 is not needed. Use 能不能…, not 能不能…嗎.

right.pinyin: Wǒ néng bù néng yòng nà jiān jiàoshì?

subsections.title: Rules and Permission (Allowed / Not Allowed)

subsections.title: Circumstances and Schedules (Possible / Not Possible)

text.traditional: 可是這些時間我都有語言交換，不能去。
text.simplified: 可是这些时间我都有语言交换，不能去。
text.pinyin: Kěshì zhèxiē shíjiān wǒ dōu yǒu yǔyán jiāohuàn, bù néng qù.
text.english: But I have language exchange then, so I cannot go.

text.traditional: 別的時間可以嗎？
text.simplified: 别的时间可以吗？
text.pinyin: Biéde shíjiān kěyǐ ma?
text.english: Could you use another time?

text.traditional: 我朋友最近比較忙，別的時間他沒有空。
text.simplified: 我朋友最近比较忙，别的时间他没有空。
text.pinyin: Wǒ péngyǒu zuìjìn bǐjiào máng, biéde shíjiān tā méi yǒukòng.

text.simplified: 我们去问老师，也许他可以帮你。
text.pinyin: Wǒmen qù wèn lǎoshī, yěxǔ tā kěyǐ bāng nǐ.

items.title: Grammar 1–3 · People, descriptions, and care advice

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Connect a Person to an Action with 跟
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Use 跟 to do things together with someone, to speak or request from someone, and to learn or borrow from someone.
grammarPages.explanation: 跟 connects you with another person. Use it to do things together (“with”), to talk or ask (“to”), or to learn or borrow (“from”). If you need a helping verb or an adverb, put it before 跟.

lessonWorld.title: Send the right care message
lessonWorld.prompt: Yuanzhen needs to pass the teacher’s advice to Guoan.
lessonWorld.traditional: 老師要我跟國安說幾句話。
lessonWorld.simplified: 老师要我跟国安说几句话。
lessonWorld.pinyin: Lǎoshī yào wǒ gēn Guó’ān shuō jǐ jù huà.
lessonWorld.english: The teacher wants me to say a few things to Guoan.

teachingGlossary.meaning: links a description to a noun
ending word: a change or a finish

grammarPages.pattern: 和…一起 ｜ 對…說話／請假 ｜ 向…學習／借

patternRows.english: Tonight I will eat with a friend.
He speaks English with his family.
I learn calligraphy from Teacher Li.

items.question: I go to the hospital with my friend — where does 跟 go?
items.answer: Right before the person who joins you: 跟朋友. The person never comes before 跟.

right.english: I go to the hospital with my friend.

items.question: I tell my friend something — where does my friend go?
items.answer: The person you tell comes right after 跟, before the action word: 我跟朋友說。

right.english: I speak to my friend.

items.question: Can 和 do the same job as 跟?
items.answer: 和 lists two people as equals — “my friend and I”. 跟 connects the person to your action: go WITH, speak TO.

right.english: I speak Chinese with the doctor.

discoveryLab.title: Move 跟, move the connection
discoveryLab.description: The same people can join different parts of the event.

choices.label: Go together
choices.pinyin: Wǒ gēn péngyǒu qù yīyuàn.
choices.english: I go to the hospital with my friend.
choices.note: 跟朋友 goes with 去醫院: the friend joins the trip.

choices.label: Talk there
choices.pinyin: Wǒ qù yīyuàn gēn péngyǒu shuōhuà.
choices.english: I go to the hospital to speak with my friend.
choices.note: Here 跟朋友 goes with 說話, not the trip.

choices.label: Tell the teacher
choices.pinyin: Wǒ xiān gēn lǎoshī qǐngjià.
choices.english: I first ask the teacher for leave.
choices.note: 老師 receives the request.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Read 跟 with the person and the action after it.

text.traditional: 今天晚上我要跟朋友吃飯。
text.simplified: 今天晚上我要跟朋友吃饭。
text.pinyin: Jīntiān wǎnshang wǒ yào gēn péngyǒu chīfàn.
text.english: Tonight I am going to eat dinner with a friend.

text.traditional: 我常常跟他一起去百貨公司買東西。
text.simplified: 我常常跟他一起去百货公司买东西。
text.pinyin: Wǒ chángcháng gēn tā yìqǐ qù bǎihuò gōngsī mǎi dōngxi.
text.english: I often go to the department store together with him to buy things.

text.traditional: 我喜歡跟家人去海邊玩。
text.simplified: 我喜欢跟家人去海边玩。
text.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuān gēn jiārén qù hǎibiān wán.
text.english: I like going to the beach with my family.

text.traditional: 他跟家人說英文，跟同學說中文。
text.simplified: 他跟家人说英文，跟同学说中文。
text.pinyin: Tā gēn jiārén shuō Yīngwén, gēn tóngxué shuō Zhōngwén.
text.english: He speaks English to his family and Chinese to his classmates.

text.traditional: 計程車司機跟我說：「去機場 1,200 塊錢。」
text.simplified: 计程车司机跟我说：「去机场 1,200 块钱。」
text.pinyin: Jìchéngchē sījī gēn wǒ shuō: "Qù jīchǎng 1,200 kuài qián."
text.english: The taxi driver said to me: "Going to the airport is 1,200 dollars."

text.traditional: 我明天不能來上課，今天要先跟老師請假。
text.simplified: 我明天不能来上课，今天要先跟老师请假。
text.pinyin: Wǒ míngtiān bù néng lái shàngkè, jīntiān yào xiān gēn lǎoshī qǐngjià.
text.english: I cannot attend class tomorrow, so today I need to ask the teacher for leave first.

words.pinyin: wǒ míngtiān bù néng lái shàngkè
words.meaning: I cannot come to class tomorrow

examples.teachingNote: 跟...學 means to learn from someone.

text.traditional: 我跟李老師學書法。
text.simplified: 我跟李老师学书法。
text.pinyin: Wǒ gēn Lǐ lǎoshī xué shūfǎ.
text.english: I learn calligraphy from Teacher Li.

examples.teachingNote: 跟...要錢 means to ask for money from parents.

text.traditional: 他二十歲了，不跟爸媽要錢了。
text.simplified: 他二十岁了，不跟爸妈要钱了。
text.pinyin: Tā èrshí suì le, bù gēn bàmā yào qián le.
text.english: He is twenty years old; he no longer asks his parents for money.

examples.teachingNote: 跟...買舊車 means to buy a used car from a friend.

text.traditional: 我不想跟朋友買舊車，我想買新車。
text.simplified: 我不想跟朋友买旧车，我想买新车。
text.pinyin: Wǒ bù xiǎng gēn péngyǒu mǎi jiù chē, wǒ xiǎng mǎi xīn chē.
text.english: I don't want to buy a used car from a friend; I want to buy a new car.

subsections.title: Doing Things with Someone (With)
subsections.explanation: Put 跟 before the person you do an activity with, like “have dinner with friends” or “go shopping with him.”

patternRows.english: Tonight I will eat with a friend.

subsections.title: Talking to Someone (To)
subsections.explanation: Put 跟 before the person you are talking to, like “he speaks English to his family” or “asking the teacher for time off.”

patternRows.english: He speaks English with his family.

subsections.title: Learning or Getting from Someone (From)
subsections.explanation: Put 跟 before the person you learn or receive something from, like “learn calligraphy from Teacher Li” or “borrow money from a friend.”

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Describe a Noun with an Action or Phrase Using 的
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Identify a person or thing by describing it first.
grammarPages.explanation: Put your whole description first, add 的, then name the person or thing: Description + 的 + Noun. To point out someone specific, add 這 (this) or 那 (that) right after 的.

lessonWorld.title: Find the person who needs help
lessonWorld.prompt: Several people are waiting. Which person has a cold?
lessonWorld.traditional: 請找感冒的人。
lessonWorld.simplified: 请找感冒的人。
lessonWorld.pinyin: Qǐng zhǎo gǎnmào de rén.
lessonWorld.english: Find the person who has a cold.

teachingGlossary.meaning: links a description to a noun
ending word: a change or a finish

grammarPages.pattern: Description + 的 + noun

patternRows.english: The characters I wrote.
The person who has a cold.
This doctor wearing a mask.

items.question: The person who has a cold — which word comes last?
items.answer: The person. Put the description first, then 的, then the person: 感冒的人。

right.english: the person who has a cold

words.meaning: links a description to a noun

items.question: Do I always need 的 between the description and the person?
items.answer: Yes. 的 is the link: description + 的 + person. Without it, the words do not join into one label.

right.english: the doctor wearing a mask

words.meaning: links a description to a noun

items.question: The medicine the doctor gave — where does 的 go?
items.answer: Right after the action word, before the thing: 醫生給的藥。The whole description stays before 的.

right.english: the medicine the doctor gave

words.meaning: links a description to a noun

discoveryLab.title: Change the label, find someone new
discoveryLab.description: The noun stays last. Everything before 的 tells you which one.

choices.label: Has a cold
choices.pinyin: gǎnmào de rén
choices.english: the person who has a cold
choices.note: 感冒 identifies the person.

choices.label: Wears a mask
choices.pinyin: dài kǒuzhào de rén
choices.english: the person wearing a mask
choices.note: The whole action 戴口罩 identifies the person.

choices.label: Mask-wearing doctor
choices.pinyin: dài kǒuzhào de yīshēng
choices.english: the doctor wearing a mask
choices.note: Changing the final noun changes who the label identifies.

choices.label: Repair the order
choices.traditional: 人感冒的 → 感冒的人
choices.simplified: 人感冒的 → 感冒的人
choices.pinyin: rén gǎnmào de → gǎnmào de rén
choices.english: Move the description before 的 and the noun.
choices.note: Chinese builds the label first, then names the noun.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Ask: “Which person or thing?” Put the answer before 的.

examples.teachingNote: The modifying clause 媽媽買 comes before 的 and the noun 蘋果 closes the phrase.

text.traditional: 媽媽買的蘋果非常好吃。
text.simplified: 妈妈买的苹果非常好吃。
text.pinyin: Māma mǎi de píngguǒ fēicháng hǎochī.
text.english: The apple Mom bought is very delicious.

examples.teachingNote: 他唱 modifies the noun 歌.

text.traditional: 他唱的歌很好聽，是哪國歌？
text.simplified: 他唱的歌很好听，是哪国歌？
text.pinyin: Tā chàng de gē hěn hǎotīng, shì nǎ guó gē?
text.english: The song he sings sounds very nice; which country's song is it?

examples.teachingNote: 他們說 modifies the noun 話.

text.traditional: 我不懂他們說的話，你懂嗎？
text.simplified: 我不懂他们说的话，你懂吗？
text.pinyin: Wǒ bù dǒng tāmen shuō de huà, nǐ dǒng ma?
text.english: I don't understand the words they are saying; do you understand?

examples.teachingNote: 在台北坐捷運 modifies 人 as a category of people.

text.traditional: 在台北坐捷運的人很多。
text.simplified: 在台北坐捷运的人很多。
text.pinyin: Zài Táiběi zuò jiéyùn de rén hěn duō.
text.english: People who take the MRT in Taipei are many.

examples.teachingNote: 會說中文 modifies 人.

text.traditional: 會說中文的人不一定會教中文。
text.simplified: 会说中文的人不一定会教中文。
text.pinyin: Huì shuō Zhōngwén de rén bù yídìng huì jiāo Zhōngwén.
text.english: People who can speak Chinese do not necessarily know how to teach Chinese.

examples.teachingNote: 常常生病 modifies 人.

text.traditional: 常常生病的人要注意身體健康。
text.simplified: 常常生病的人要注意身体健康。
text.pinyin: Chángcháng shēngbìng de rén yào zhùyì shēntǐ jiànkāng.
text.english: People who get sick often need to pay attention to their health.

examples.teachingNote: Clause 我太太買 precedes 的那件衣服 (Dem + M + N).

text.traditional: 我太太買的那件衣服好貴！
text.simplified: 我太太买的那件衣服好贵！
text.pinyin: Wǒ tàitai mǎi de nà jiàn yīfu hǎoguì!
text.english: That piece of clothing my wife bought is so expensive!

examples.teachingNote: Clause 你問 precedes 的這兩個問題 (Dem + Num + M + N).

text.traditional: 你問的這兩個問題都非常難。
text.simplified: 你问的这两个问题都非常难。
text.pinyin: Nǐ wèn de zhè liǎng ge wèntí dōu fēicháng nán.
text.english: These two questions that you asked are both extremely difficult.

examples.teachingNote: Clause 在跳舞 precedes 的那些學生.

text.traditional: 在跳舞的那些學生都是我的朋友。
text.simplified: 在跳舞的那些学生都是我的朋友。
text.pinyin: Zài tiàowǔ de nàxiē xuéshēng dōu shì wǒ de péngyǒu.
text.english: Those students who are dancing are all my friends.

grammarPages.titleTraditional: 把行動調多一點或少一點
grammarPages.titleEnglish: Do an Action More or Less
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Give useful advice with 多 or 少 before an action.
grammarPages.explanation: Put 多 or 少 before the action you want someone to increase or reduce.

lessonWorld.title: Adjust the advice
lessonWorld.prompt: Guoan needs more water and rest, but less phone time.
lessonWorld.traditional: 你應該多喝水、少看手機。
lessonWorld.simplified: 你应该多喝水、少看手机。
lessonWorld.pinyin: Nǐ yīnggāi duō hē shuǐ, shǎo kàn shǒujī.
lessonWorld.english: You should drink more water and look at your phone less.

teachingGlossary.meaning: links a description to a noun
ending word: a change or a finish

grammarPages.pattern: 多／少 + action

patternRows.english: Exercise more.
drink more water
rest more
look at the phone less

items.question: Why can’t I just say 多水 for “more water”?
items.answer: 多 and 少 adjust an action word. Water is a thing, so add the action first: 多喝水。

right.english: Drink more water.

items.question: Does 多 come before or after the action?
items.answer: Before it: 多休息, 少看手機. Never after the action word.

right.english: Rest more.

items.question: How do I say “drink MORE water” as advice?
items.answer: 很多水 means “a lot of water”. For advice to drink more, put 多 right before the action: 多喝水。

right.english: You should drink more water.

discoveryLab.title: Turn the action up or down
discoveryLab.description: 多 and 少 change how often or how much the action happens.

choices.label: More water
choices.pinyin: Duō hē shuǐ.
choices.english: Drink more water.
choices.note: 多 sits before the action 喝.

choices.label: More rest
choices.pinyin: Duō xiūxi.
choices.english: Rest more.
choices.note: The advice increases the action.

choices.label: Less phone
choices.pinyin: Shǎo kàn shǒujī.
choices.english: Look at your phone less.
choices.note: 少 reduces 看手機.

choices.label: Repair the advice
choices.pinyin: duō shuǐ → duō hē shuǐ
choices.english: Add the missing action.
choices.note: Water is a thing. Health advice needs the action 喝.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Choose an action first. Put 多 or 少 directly before it.

examples.teachingNote: One action goes up, one goes down.

text.traditional: 你應該多運動，少喝一點兒酒。
text.simplified: 你应该多运动，少喝一点儿酒。
text.pinyin: Nǐ yīnggāi duō yùndòng, shǎo hē yìdiǎnr jiǔ.
text.english: You should exercise more and drink a little less alcohol.

examples.teachingNote: Source health advice.

text.traditional: 我發燒了，醫生跟我說要多喝水、多休息、少看手機。
text.simplified: 我发烧了，医生跟我说要多喝水、多休息、少看手机。
text.pinyin: Wǒ fāshāo le, yīshēng gēn wǒ shuō yào duō hē shuǐ, duō xiūxi, shǎo kàn shǒujī.
text.english: I have a fever; the doctor told me to drink more water, rest more, and look at my phone less.

words.meaning: ending word: a change or a finish

examples.teachingNote: 多 changes 休息.

text.traditional: 生病的時候要多休息。
text.simplified: 生病的时候要多休息。
text.pinyin: Shēngbìng de shíhòu yào duō xiūxi.
text.english: When sick, rest more.

words.meaning: links a description to a noun

examples.teachingNote: The pattern can repeat across several actions.

text.traditional: 我們學習語言，平常應該要多聽、多說、多寫、多練習。
text.simplified: 我们学习语言，平常应该要多听、多说、多写、多练习。
text.pinyin: Wǒmen xuéxí yǔyán, píngcháng yīnggāi yào duō tīng, duō shuō, duō xiě, duō liànxí.
text.english: When we learn a language, we should listen, speak, write, and practice more in daily life.

dialogue.title: 對話一 · Dialogue 1
dialogue.setting: 在學校 · At school

text.traditional: 老師，國安今天要請假。他發燒了，不能來上課。
text.simplified: 老师，国安今天要请假。他发烧了，不能来上课。
text.pinyin: Lǎoshī, Guó’ān jīntiān yào qǐngjià. Tā fāshāo le, bù néng lái shàngkè.
text.english: Teacher, Guoan has to take a leave today. He has a fever and he can’t come to school.

words.meaning: ending word: a change or a finish

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Use 會 for an Expected Future
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say what you expect will happen.
grammarPages.explanation: With a future time, 會 introduces the action you expect. Put the time before 會.

lessonWorld.title: Promise a visit
lessonWorld.prompt: Yuanzhen tells Guoan what she plans to do tomorrow.

lessonWorld.simplified: 我明天会带水果去看你。

grammarPages.pattern: Time + person + 會 + action

patternRows.english: I will come tomorrow.
The doctor will speak tomorrow.
He will go to the hospital tomorrow.

items.question: I will come tomorrow — where does 明天 go?
items.answer: Before 會. Time first, then 會 + the action: 我明天會來。

right.english: I will come tomorrow.

items.question: Does 會 mean “can” or “will”?
items.answer: With no time word, 會 can read as a skill: 我會說中文 is “I can speak Chinese”. Add a time word and it reads as “will”.

right.english: I will go to the hospital tomorrow.

items.question: For “I will visit you tomorrow”, can I use 可以?
items.answer: 可以 says you are allowed or able. For something you expect to happen, use 會.

right.pinyin: Wǒ míngtiān huì qù kàn nǐ.
right.english: I will visit you tomorrow.

discoveryLab.title: Let the time choose the meaning
discoveryLab.description: 會 can describe ability or an expected future. Look for the time clue.

choices.label: Ability
choices.pinyin: Wǒ huì shuō Zhōngwén.
choices.english: I can speak Chinese.
choices.note: No future time here; 會 means a learned skill.

choices.label: Tomorrow
choices.pinyin: Wǒ míngtiān huì lái.
choices.english: I will come tomorrow.
choices.note: 明天 makes this an expected future.

choices.label: Visit Guoan
choices.pinyin: Wǒ míngtiān huì qù kàn Guó’ān.
choices.english: I will visit Guoan tomorrow.
choices.note: Time first, then 會 + action.

choices.label: Repair the order
choices.traditional: 我會明天去 → 我明天會去
choices.simplified: 我会明天去 → 我明天会去
choices.pinyin: wǒ huì míngtiān qù → wǒ míngtiān huì qù
choices.english: Move the time before 會.
choices.note: The future time frames the whole action.

discoveryLab.takeaway: A future time before 會 helps the listener read it as “will.”

text.simplified: 我今天会去百货公司帮你买。

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Connect a Condition and Result
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say what should happen if a condition becomes true.
grammarPages.explanation: 如果 or 要是 opens the condition. 就 clearly points to the result that follows. If both parts have the same subject, you can leave the second one out.

lessonWorld.title: Prepare for a change
lessonWorld.prompt: The doctor explains what Guoan should do if the fever returns.
lessonWorld.traditional: 如果發燒了，就吃紅色的藥。
lessonWorld.simplified: 如果发烧了，就吃红色的药。
lessonWorld.pinyin: Rúguǒ fāshāo le, jiù chī hóngsè de yào.
lessonWorld.english: If you develop a fever, take the red medicine.

teachingGlossary.meaning: links a description to a noun
ending word: a change or a finish

grammarPages.pattern: 如果／要是 + condition， 就 + result

patternRows.english: If he does not go, we will not go either.
If you want to eat, eat a bit more!

items.question: Where does 就 go in an if-then sentence?
items.answer: 就 starts the result, after the condition. It never sits inside the condition.

right.english: If you have a fever, then take medicine.

items.question: In the fever sentence, where does 了 go?
items.answer: 了 goes right after the action word that marks the change: 發燒了. At the very end it would change the sentence into a new decision, not a health instruction.

right.pinyin: Rúguǒ fāshāo le, jiù chī yào.
right.english: If you develop a fever, take medicine.

words.meaning: ending word: a change or a finish

items.question: Can I say the result first, like in English?
items.answer: No — the condition comes first, then 就 + the result: IF this, THEN that. 要是 works the same as 如果.

right.english: If you have a fever, then rest.

discoveryLab.title: Change the condition, change the result
discoveryLab.description: The left side opens a possible situation. 就 points to the response.

choices.label: Fever
choices.pinyin: Rúguǒ fāshāo, jiù chī yào.
choices.english: If you have a fever, take medicine.
choices.note: 發燒 is the condition; 吃藥 is the response.

choices.label: Unwell
choices.traditional: 如果不舒服，就去看醫生。
choices.simplified: 如果不舒服，就去看医生。
choices.pinyin: Rúguǒ bù shūfu, jiù qù kàn yīshēng.
choices.english: If you feel unwell, see a doctor.
choices.note: 就 makes the condition-to-result link explicit.

choices.label: Cold weather
choices.pinyin: Yàoshi tiānqì lěng, jiù dài kǒuzhào.
choices.english: If the weather is cold, wear a mask.
choices.note: 要是 works like 如果 in this pattern.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Think in two boxes: IF this becomes true → THEN do this.

ruleContrast.title: Clearer link, not a fake error
ruleContrast.description: Mandarin advice can leave out 就. The full book pattern makes the condition and result easier to see.

items.title: Grammar 1–3 · Completed, unfinished, and focused past events

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: How Did You Meet Each Other?
grammarPages.titleEnglish: Completed Action with 了
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say that an action is finished.
grammarPages.explanation: Put 了 right after a verb to mark a completed action. With amounts, one 了 means the action stopped there; adding a second 了 at the end means the action probably continues.

lessonWorld.title: Rebuild the chat history
lessonWorld.prompt: Yiwen asks whether Youmei completed today’s homework.
lessonWorld.traditional: 功課妳寫了嗎？
lessonWorld.simplified: 功课你写了吗？
lessonWorld.pinyin: Gōngkè nǐ xiě le ma?
lessonWorld.english: Did you finish the homework?

teachingGlossary.meaning: links an action word to how it was done

grammarPages.pattern: Verb + object or amount + 了

patternRows.english: I completed the homework.
I drank it.
Dad bought it.

items.question: Where does 了 go in “I wrote the homework yesterday”?
items.answer: Right after the action word. 了 follows 寫, before the homework.

right.english: I wrote the homework yesterday.

items.question: Do I need 了 for something I do every day?
items.answer: No. 了 marks one finished action. For a habit you repeat, leave 了 out.

right.english: I drink coffee every day.

items.question: How do I say “I am writing a card” right now?
items.answer: Use 在 before the action word. 了 would say the card is already done.

right.english: I am writing a card.

discoveryLab.title: Watch the action reach DONE
discoveryLab.description: The picture—not the English time words—shows whether the action is happening now or already finished.

choices.label: General action
choices.pinyin: Wǒ xiě gōngkè.
choices.english: I do homework.
choices.note: The sentence names the activity. It does not say if it is happening now or finished.

choices.label: Happening now
choices.pinyin: Wǒ zài xiě gōngkè.
choices.english: I am doing homework now.
choices.note: 在 shows the action is happening now.

choices.label: Completed
choices.pinyin: Wǒ xiě le gōngkè.
choices.english: I completed the homework.
choices.note: 了 shows the action is finished.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Ask: is the action general, happening now, or finished?

examples.teachingNote: Single 了 after V(O) indicates a completed action in the past.

text.traditional: 他已經去上課了。
text.simplified: 他已经去上课了。
text.pinyin: Tā yǐjīng qù shàngkè le.
text.english: He has already gone to class.

examples.teachingNote: 今天早上去看醫生了 indicates the visit is completed.

text.traditional: 我今天早上去看醫生了。
text.simplified: 我今天早上去看医生了。
text.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān zǎoshang qù kàn yīshēng le.
text.english: I went to see the doctor this morning.

examples.teachingNote: 都寫功課了 confirms the homework is finished.

text.traditional: 我跟弟弟都寫功課了。
text.simplified: 我跟弟弟都写功课了。
text.pinyin: Wǒ gēn dìdi dōu xiě gōngkè le.
text.english: My younger brother and I have both finished our homework.

examples.teachingNote: Comparative pair: (a) Single 了 for past completed quantity; (b) Double 了 indicates so far, with more likely to come.

text.traditional: 我上個禮拜學了十個中國字。我已經學了四百多個中國字了。
text.simplified: 我上个礼拜学了十个中国字。我已经学了四百多个中国字了。
text.pinyin: Wǒ shàng ge lǐbài xué le shí ge Zhōngguózì. Wǒ yǐjīng xué le sìbǎi duō ge Zhōngguózì le.
text.english: I learned ten Chinese characters last week. I have already learned more than 400 Chinese characters so far.

examples.teachingNote: Comparative pair: (a) Single 了 for buying a car; (b) Double 了 indicates he already bought one and still wants another.

text.traditional: 爸爸上個月買了一輛新車。爸爸已經買了一輛新車了，還想再買一輛。
text.simplified: 爸爸上个月买了一辆新车。爸爸已经买了一辆新车了，还想再买一辆。
text.pinyin: Bàba shàng ge yuè mǎi le yí liàng xīn chē. Bàba yǐjīng mǎi le yí liàng xīn chē le, hái xiǎng zài mǎi yí liàng.

items.question: He did not come yesterday — 沒 or 還沒?
items.answer: 沒. Yesterday is finished, so the chance to come is over. 還沒 is for something still waiting to happen.

items.question: “How did you meet?” — do I answer with 了?
items.answer: No. The question asks how, so 是…的 puts the spotlight on the way you met. 了 alone would only say it happened.

items.question: Where does the detail go in a 是…的 sentence?
items.answer: Between 是 and the action word. The way you met comes before 認識.

items.question: Do I need the 的 at the end?
items.answer: Yes. 是…的 works as a pair. Without the ending 的, the sentence loses its spotlight.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: How Did You Meet Each Other?
grammarPages.titleEnglish: Put Steps in Order with 先…等…再…
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Explain a plan where you do one thing, wait, then do another.
grammarPages.explanation: 先 starts the first action. 等 names what you wait for. 再 starts the later action. With 再 alone, the action is not happening now — it waits for a later time. With 等, the second action waits until the first one happens.

teachingGlossary.meaning: links an action word to how it was done

grammarPages.pattern: 先 + first action，等 + condition，再 + later action

items.question: Which step does 先 start?
items.answer: 先 starts the first action. 等 names what you wait for, and 再 starts the later action.

items.question: Is it 在 or 再 for the later step?
items.answer: 再. It means “then; after that”. 在 talks about where something is.

right.english: Decide first, then arrange a time.

items.question: Can 再 start the first step?
items.answer: No. 再 belongs to the later action. 先 opens the plan.

choices.pinyin: Xiān xiǎng yì xiǎng, děng nǐ juédìng le, zài gěi wǒ dǎ diànhuà.
choices.english: Think first; when you decide, call me.
choices.note: The call waits for the decision.

discoveryLab.takeaway: 先 starts it. 等 waits for it. 再 moves to the later action.

examples.teachingNote: The first step is left out; the wait is named.

text.traditional: 等她起床了，你再跟她說。
text.simplified: 等她起床了，你再跟她说。
text.pinyin: Děng tā qǐchuáng le, nǐ zài gēn tā shuō.
text.english: Wait until she wakes up, then you can tell her.

examples.teachingNote: What you wait for comes after 等.

text.traditional: 天氣太冷了，等車來了，我們再去外面。
text.simplified: 天气太冷了，等车来了，我们再去外面。
text.pinyin: Tiānqì tài lěng le, děng chē lái le, wǒmen zài qù wàimiàn.
text.english: It is too cold; wait for the car, then go back outside.

examples.teachingNote: All three stages appear.

text.traditional: 先做功課，等爸爸回家了，再一起吃晚飯。
text.simplified: 先做功课，等爸爸回家了，再一起吃晚饭。
text.pinyin: Xiān zuò gōngkè, děng bàba huí jiā le, zài yìqǐ chī wǎnfàn.
text.english: Do homework first; when Dad returns, eat dinner together.

examples.teachingNote: A fun example from the book.

text.traditional: 對啊，我們先去吃冰淇淋，等不熱了，再去海邊玩，好不好？
text.simplified: 对啊，我们先去吃冰淇淋，等不热了，再去海边玩，好不好？
text.pinyin: Duì a, wǒmen xiān qù chī bīngqílín, děng bú rè le, zài qù hǎibiān wán, hǎo bù hǎo?
text.english: Right — let us go eat ice cream first, and when it is not so hot, then go play at the beach, okay?

text.traditional: 這家餐廳今天人太多了，我們以後再來吧。
text.simplified: 这家餐厅今天人太多了，我们以后再来吧。
text.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng jīntiān rén tài duō le, wǒmen yǐhòu zài lái ba.
text.english: This restaurant has too many people today; let us come again another time.

text.traditional: A：爸爸，這個句子是什麼意思？ B：我現在沒空，晚上再告訴你。
text.simplified: A：爸爸，这个句子是什么意思？ B：我现在没空，晚上再告诉你。
text.pinyin: A: Bàba, zhège jùzi shì shénme yìsi? B: Wǒ xiànzài méi kòng, wǎnshang zài gàosù nǐ.
text.english: A: Dad, what does this sentence mean? B: I have no time now; I will tell you tonight.

text.traditional: A：你要不要跟我一起去打球？ B：我今天有一點兒累，我們週末再去吧。
text.simplified: A：你要不要跟我一起去打球？ B：我今天有一点儿累，我们周末再去吧。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ yào bú yào gēn wǒ yìqǐ qù dǎqiú? B: Wǒ jīntiān yǒu yìdiǎnr lèi, wǒmen zhōumò zài qù ba.
text.english: A: Do you want to play ball with me? B: I am a little tired today; let us go on the weekend.

text.traditional: 等我先生也喝了，我們再決定買不買。
text.simplified: 等我先生也喝了，我们再决定买不买。
text.pinyin: Děng wǒ xiānsheng yě hē le, wǒmen zài juédìng mǎi bù mǎi.
text.english: Wait until my husband has also drunk some; then we will decide whether to buy it.

text.traditional: 等下了課再教你，好不好？
text.simplified: 等下了课再教你，好不好？
text.pinyin: Děng xià le kè zài jiāo nǐ, hǎo bù hǎo?
text.english: Wait until class is over and then I will teach you, okay?

text.traditional: 現在去吃飯的人太多了，我想先寫功課，等人少了再去吃。
text.simplified: 现在去吃饭的人太多了，我想先写功课，等人少了再去吃。
text.pinyin: Xiànzài qù chīfàn de rén tài duō le, wǒ xiǎng xiān xiě gōngkè, děng rén shǎo le zài qù chī.
text.english: Too many people are eating now; I want to do my homework first, and go eat when there are fewer people.

text.traditional: 我要先去朋友家，等百貨公司開了，再去買衣服。

text.english: I will go to my friend’s place first; when the department store opens, I will go buy clothes.

wait until the department store opens

items.question: “Write a card to a friend” — 給 or 跟?
items.answer: 給. The friend gets the card. 跟 goes with someone — like meeting or chatting together.

right.english: I write a card to my friend.

items.question: Where does the person who gets it go?
items.answer: Right after 給, before the action. 給 + person + action.

right.english: I write a card to my friend.

items.question: How do I say “my brother did not call me”?
items.answer: Put 給我 before 打電話. The person who gets the call comes right after 給.

right.pinyin: Gēge méi gěi wǒ dǎ diànhuà.
right.english: My older brother did not call me.

text.english: I want to write her a letter.

text.traditional: 妳跟那位新朋友見面了沒有？
text.simplified: 你跟那位新朋友见面了没有？
text.pinyin: Nǐ gēn nà wèi xīn péngyǒu jiànmiàn le méiyǒu?
text.english: Have you met up with your new friend yet?

text.traditional: 我還沒決定要不要跟他見面。
text.simplified: 我还没决定要不要跟他见面。
text.pinyin: Wǒ hái méi juédìng yào bú yào gēn tā jiànmiàn.
text.english: I haven’t decided to meet him or not.

text.traditional: 妳擔心什麼？
text.simplified: 你担心什么？
text.pinyin: Nǐ dānxīn shénme?
text.english: What are you worried about?

text.traditional: 我有點兒緊張，我以前沒有這種經驗，所以覺得這樣有點兒奇怪。
text.simplified: 我有点儿紧张，我以前没有这种经验，所以觉得这样有点儿奇怪。
text.pinyin: Wǒ yǒudiǎnr jǐnzhāng, wǒ yǐqián méiyǒu zhè zhǒng jīngyàn, suǒyǐ juéde zhèyàng yǒudiǎnr qíguài.
text.english: I am a little nervous. I have never had an experience like this before, so I think it is a little strange.

text.traditional: 妳不要緊張，我有辦法，我跟妳一起去。
text.simplified: 你不要紧张，我有办法，我跟你一起去。
text.pinyin: Nǐ bú yào jǐnzhāng, wǒ yǒu bànfǎ, wǒ gēn nǐ yìqǐ qù.
text.english: Don’t be nervous. I have an idea: I can be there for you.

text.traditional: 太好了，謝謝妳幫我的忙。
text.simplified: 太好了，谢谢你帮我的忙。
text.pinyin: Tài hǎo le, xièxie nǐ bāng wǒ de máng.
text.english: Great! Thank you for helping me.

text.traditional: 不客氣。妳打算什麼時候跟他見面？
text.simplified: 不客气。你打算什么时候跟他见面？
text.pinyin: Bú kèqi. Nǐ dǎsuàn shénme shíhou gēn tā jiànmiàn?
text.english: You’re welcome. When do you plan to meet him?

text.traditional: 可能這個週末吧。如果妳有空，我再跟他約時間。
text.simplified: 可能这个周末吧。如果你有空，我再跟他约时间。
text.pinyin: Kěnéng zhège zhōumò ba. Rúguǒ nǐ yǒukòng, wǒ zài gēn tā yuē shíjiān.
text.english: Maybe this weekend. If you are free, I will arrange a time with him.

text.traditional: 有空啊，但是我明天不會來學校，等妳決定了，再給我打電話吧。
text.simplified: 有空啊，但是我明天不会来学校，等你决定了，再给我打电话吧。
text.pinyin: Yǒukòng a, dànshì wǒ míngtiān bú huì lái xuéxiào, děng nǐ juédìng le, zài gěi wǒ dǎ diànhuà ba.
text.english: I am free, but I won’t come to school tomorrow. When you decide, call me.

grammarPages.pattern: Person + 用 + tool + action

patternRows.english: I like to write letters in Chinese.
I take photos using my phone.

items.question: I write letters using Chinese. Where does 中文 go?
items.answer: 中文 is the tool, so it goes right after 用, before the action: 用中文寫信.

right.english: I write letters using Chinese.

items.question: Can you write with a brush — do I still need 用?
items.answer: Yes. 用 stays between 會 and the tool: 會用毛筆寫字. English drops the word “use”; Chinese does not.

right.pinyin: Nǐ huì yòng máobǐ xiě zì ma?
right.english: Can you write characters with a brush?

items.question: I chat with friends in Chinese — 用 or 跟 before 中文?
items.answer: 用. 用 names the language or tool. 跟 is for the person you do it with: 跟朋友.

right.pinyin: Wǒ yòng Zhōngwén gēn péngyǒu liáotiān.
right.english: I chat with friends in Chinese.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Place 以前 and 以後 on the Timeline
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Use 以前 and 以後 as standalone time words, after specific times, and after action statements.
grammarPages.explanation: 以前 means “before” or “in the past”; 以後 means “after” or “in the future.” You can use them on their own, or put them right after a time or an activity.

grammarPages.pattern: 獨立時間詞 ｜ 時間點＋以前／以後 ｜ 句子＋以前／以後

patternRows.english: He was previously a teacher.

complement.meaning: I must arrive at the bank

items.question: I go home before three. Where does 以前 go?
items.answer: Right after the time: 三點以前. 我以前三點回家 means something else — “I used to go home at three.”

right.pinyin: Wǒ sān diǎn yǐqián huí jiā.
right.english: I go home before three.

items.question: I want to be a reporter after graduating. Where does 以後 go?
items.answer: Right after the event: 畢業以後. Put it before the event and 以後畢業 means “graduate later.”

right.english: After graduating, I will become a reporter.

items.question: I want to be a reporter someday. Is 半年以後 okay?
items.answer: No. 半年以後 means “six months from now.” For a someday plan, use plain 以後.

right.english: I will become a reporter someday.

discoveryLab.title: Move 以前 and change the meaning
discoveryLab.description: Both sentences are correct. Position tells the listener what 以前 belongs to.

choices.label: Used to
choices.pinyin: Wǒ yǐqián sān diǎn huí jiā.
choices.english: I used to go home at three.
choices.note: 以前 points broadly to a previous period of life.

items.question: The boss is kind to me. Why does 我 come so early?
items.answer: 對 points at the receiver, so 我 follows it right away: 對我好. English puts “to me” at the end; Chinese does not.

items.question: My coworkers are kind to me. Did I say it right with 我對同事很好?
items.answer: No — you turned the arrow around. The person right after 對 receives the kindness, so it is 同事對我很好.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Mark a Life Experience with 過
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Talk about past experiences with 過 and state completed actions with 過了.
grammarPages.explanation: Use 過 right after a verb to talk about life experience: something you have done before. Pairing it with final 了 relates it closely to now — you already did it, so you do not need to again. V過了 (with final 了) is only used in positive or question forms — in a negative sentence say 沒 + verb + 過 (我還沒吃過).

text.traditional: 很多台灣人去過日本，因為從台灣到日本不遠。
text.simplified: 很多台湾人去过日本，因为从台湾到日本不远。

text.english: Many Taiwanese have been to Japan, because it is not far from Taiwan to Japan.

text.traditional: A：他來過我們家嗎？ B：來過，那個時候你不在家。
text.simplified: A：他来过我们家吗？ B：来过，那个时候你不在家。
text.pinyin: A: Tā láiguo wǒmen jiā ma? B: Láiguo, nàge shíhou nǐ bú zài jiā.
text.english: A: Has he ever been to our home? B: Yes, he came; you weren't home at that time.

text.traditional: A：你吃過臭豆腐嗎？ B：我還沒吃過，聽說很特別。
text.simplified: A：你吃过臭豆腐吗？ B：我还没吃过，听说很特别。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ chīguo chòudòufu ma? B: Wǒ hái méi chīguo, tīngshuō hěn tèbié.
text.english: A: Have you eaten stinky tofu? B: I haven't tried it yet; I hear it is unique.

text.traditional: A：你要跟我們一起吃午飯嗎？ B：我吃過了，你們去吃吧！
text.simplified: A：你要跟我们一起吃午饭吗？ B：我吃过了，你们去吃吧！
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ yào gēn wǒmen yìqǐ chī wǔfàn ma? B: Wǒ chīguo le, nǐmen qù chī ba!
text.english: A: Do you want to eat lunch with us? B: I've already eaten; you all go ahead!

text.traditional: A：李小姐今天要來我們公司，她來過了嗎？ B：她來過了，是早上來的。
text.simplified: A：李小姐今天要来我们公司，她来过了吗？ B：她来过了，是早上来的。
text.pinyin: A: Lǐ xiǎojiě jīntiān yào lái wǒmen gōngsī, tā láiguo le ma? B: Tā láiguo le, shì zǎoshang lái de.
text.english: A: Miss Li is visiting our company today; has she already come? B: She has already been here; she came in the morning.

text.traditional: A：他給大家寫了一張卡片，你們都看過了嗎？ B：我看過了。 C：我還沒看。
text.simplified: A：他给大家写了一张卡片，你们都看过了吗？ B：我看过了。 C：我还没看。
text.pinyin: A: Tā gěi dàjiā xiě le yì zhāng kǎpiàn, nǐmen dōu kànguo le ma? B: Wǒ kànguo le. C: Wǒ hái méi kàn.
text.english: A: He wrote a card for everyone, have you all read it yet? B: I have already read it. C: I haven't read it yet.

subsections.title: Already Done for Now (過 ... 了)

items.question: When working, I use Chinese — is it 工作時候 or 工作的時候?
items.answer: Keep 的. 的 connects the situation to 時候: 工作的時候.

right.english: When working, speak Chinese.

items.question: When I feel unhappy, I listen to music. Where does 不好 go?
items.answer: Keep the situation together: 心情不好, then 的時候. 的時候 needs the whole situation before it.

right.traditional: 心情不好的時候，聽音樂。
right.simplified: 心情不好的时候，听音乐。

right.english: When I feel unhappy, I listen to music.

items.question: I drink water while exercising. Is 運動以後 okay?
items.answer: No. 運動以後 means after exercising. For inside the moment, use 運動的時候.

right.pinyin: Yùndòng de shíhòu, wǒ hē shuǐ.
right.english: When exercising, I drink water.

dialogue.setting: 談打工經驗 · Discussing work experience

text.traditional: 國安，你每天下課以後都要去麵包店工作，辛苦嗎？
text.simplified: 国安，你每天下课以后都要去面包店工作，辛苦吗？
text.pinyin: Guó’ān, nǐ měitiān xiàkè yǐhòu dōu yào qù miànbāodiàn gōngzuò, xīnkǔ ma?
text.english: Guoan, you work at the bakery everyday after school. Is it tiring?

text.traditional: 不辛苦。我很喜歡這個工作，因為可以學怎麼做麵包，而且同事也都對我很好。
text.simplified: 不辛苦。我很喜欢这个工作，因为可以学怎么做面包，而且同事也都对我很好。
text.pinyin: Bù xīnkǔ. Wǒ hěn xǐhuān zhège gōngzuò, yīnwèi kěyǐ xué zěnme zuò miànbāo, érqiě tóngshì yě dōu duì wǒ hěn hǎo.
text.english: It’s okay. I like this job very much because I get to learn how to make bread. Moreover, the colleagues are very nice to me as well.

text.traditional: 這樣你在學校的成績，不會有問題嗎？
text.simplified: 这样你在学校的成绩，不会有问题吗？
text.pinyin: Zhèyàng nǐ zài xuéxiào de chéngjì, bú huì yǒu wèntí ma?
text.english: Does it affect your studies?

text.traditional: 不會啊！我都先做功課，再去工作。
text.simplified: 不会啊！我都先做功课，再去工作。
text.pinyin: Bú huì a! Wǒ dōu xiān zuò gōngkè, zài qù gōngzuò.
text.english: No, it doesn’t. I always do my homework first, and then go to work.

text.traditional: 我以前在餐廳上過班，因為太累了，常常睡得不夠。
text.simplified: 我以前在餐厅上过班，因为太累了，常常睡得不够。
text.pinyin: Wǒ yǐqián zài cāntīng shàngguo bān, yīnwèi tài lèi le, chángcháng shuì de bú gòu.
text.english: I have worked at a restaurant before. I was exhausted, and always didn’t get enough sleep.

lessonWorld.simplified: 你可以先看看。

lessonWorld.english: You can take a quick look first.

grammarPages.pattern: Action verb + action verb / Action verb + 一 + action verb

patternRows.english: I take a quick look at my phone.

subject.traditional: 今天不想出去，只想在家
subject.pinyin: jīntiān bù xiǎng chūqù, zhǐ xiǎng zài jiā
subject.meaning: do not want to go out today; only want to stay home

patternRows.english: I do not want to go out today. I just want to listen to music at home.
We chat for a bit.

subject.traditional: 聽說他的新房子很漂亮，
subject.simplified: 听说他的新房子很漂亮，
subject.pinyin: tīngshuō tā de xīn fángzi hěn piàoliang

items.question: Does 看看 mean I look two times?
items.answer: No. Doubling the action word makes it short and casual — “for a bit.” 兩次 counts an exact number.

right.english: I want to take a look.

items.question: 聊天 already has two parts. Can I double the whole word?
items.answer: No. Double only the first part: 聊聊天. The rest of the word stays the same.

right.english: Let us chat for a bit.

items.question: I already took a look. Is it 看看了?
items.answer: No. For a finished quick look, put 了 between the two parts: 看了看.

right.english: I took a quick look at my phone.

discoveryLab.title: Short action, not two actions
discoveryLab.description: Repeating the action word softens it. It does not count exactly twice.

choices.label: Quick look
choices.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng kànkan.
choices.english: I want to take a look.
choices.note: 看看 makes the request feel light.

choices.label: Exactly twice
choices.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng kàn liǎng cì.
choices.english: I want to look twice.
choices.note: 兩次 counts an exact number. 看看 does not.

choices.label: Listen a bit
choices.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng tīngting yīnyuè.
choices.english: I want to listen to some music.
choices.note: The action feels relaxed and limited.

choices.label: Casual chat
choices.pinyin: Wǒmen liáo liáotiān ba.
choices.english: Let us chat for a bit.
choices.note: A two-part action like 聊天 can repeat its first part in this shape.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Do not translate the repeated verb as “twice.” Hear it as “for a bit.”

examples.teachingNote: Action verb reduplication softens the tone to indicate doing something casually.

text.traditional: 他週末常去打打球、看看電影。
text.simplified: 他周末常去打打球、看看电影。
text.pinyin: Tā zhōumò cháng qù dǎdǎ qiú, kànkan diànyǐng.
text.english: On weekends he often goes to play ball and watch movies.

examples.teachingNote: Two reduplicated verbs create a relaxed, casual picture of leisure time.

text.traditional: 我平常有空的時候，都在家上上網、玩玩手機。
text.simplified: 我平常有空的时候，都在家上上网、玩玩手机。
text.pinyin: Wǒ píngcháng yǒu kòng de shíhòu, dōu zài jiā shàngshàng wǎng, wánwán shǒujī.
text.english: When I have free time usually, I go online and play on my phone at home.

examples.teachingNote: A gentle social action.

text.traditional: 媽媽最近心情不太好，我們應該多跟她說說話。
text.simplified: 妈妈最近心情不太好，我们应该多跟她说说话。
text.pinyin: Māma zuìjìn xīnqíng bú tài hǎo, wǒmen yīnggāi duō gēn tā shuō shuōhuà.
text.english: Mom has been in a bad mood lately; we should talk with her more.

examples.teachingNote: Several casual actions can form a relaxed scene.

text.traditional: 上班的休息時間，我常跟同事一起喝喝咖啡、聊聊天。
text.simplified: 上班的休息时间，我常跟同事一起喝喝咖啡、聊聊天。
text.pinyin: Shàngbān de xiūxi shíjiān, wǒ cháng gēn tóngshì yìqǐ hēhe kāfēi, liáo liáotiān.
text.english: During breaks at work, I often have coffee and chat with coworkers.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Move from a Start toward a Direction
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Give a route using a clear start and direction.
grammarPages.explanation: 從 opens the starting point. 往 opens the direction or destination you move toward.

lessonWorld.title: Get to the museum before it opens
lessonWorld.prompt: The museum is near Guoan’s home.
lessonWorld.traditional: 從我家出去，往右轉。
lessonWorld.simplified: 从我家出去，往右转。
lessonWorld.pinyin: Cóng wǒ jiā chūqù, wǎng yòu zhuǎn.
lessonWorld.english: Go out from my home and turn right.

grammarPages.pattern: 從 + start + 往 + direction + action

patternRows.english: Look from here toward the doorway.
Walk from my home toward the right.
Look forward from here.
Write from the left to the right.

items.question: I want to walk from my home toward the right. Which word is the start?
items.answer: 從 marks where you leave from; 往 marks the way you go. Put 從 first: 從我家往右邊走.

right.pinyin: Cóng wǒ jiā wǎng yòubiān zǒu.
right.english: Walk from my home toward the right.

items.question: Do I need a word before 我家 when I start moving?
items.answer: Yes — 從. It opens the starting point of the movement.

right.pinyin: Cóng wǒ jiā chūqù, wǎng yòu zhuǎn.
right.english: Go out from my home and turn right.

items.question: Can I use 到 instead of 往 for a direction?
items.answer: No. 到 means “arrive at a place.” 往 points the way you move, so use 往 for a direction.

right.english: Walk from here toward the entrance.

routeLab.title: Trace the route arrow
routeLab.description: Choose a route. The left point is 從; the arrow points 往 the destination.

choices.label: To the entrance
choices.pinyin: Cóng zhèlǐ wǎng ménkǒu zǒu.
choices.english: Walk from here toward the entrance.
choices.note: 這裡 is the start; 門口 is the direction.

choices.label: Forward
choices.pinyin: Cóng wǒ jiā wǎng qián zǒu.
choices.english: Walk forward from my home.
choices.note: 往前 gives a direction rather than a named place.

choices.label: Look outside
choices.pinyin: Cóng chuānghu wǎng wài kàn.
choices.english: Look outside from the window.
choices.note: The eyes move from the window toward outside.

routeLab.takeaway: Find the start first. Then follow 往 toward the direction.

examples.teachingNote: A writing direction.

text.traditional: 中國字應該從左往右寫，韓國字呢？
text.simplified: 中国字应该从左往右写，韩国字呢？
text.pinyin: Zhōngguó zì yīnggāi cóng zuǒ wǎng yòu xiě, Hánguó zì ne?
text.english: Chinese characters should be written from left to right. What about Korean characters?

examples.teachingNote: A source-to-view direction.

text.traditional: 從我房間的窗戶往外看，就可以看到漂亮的風景。
text.simplified: 从我房间的窗户往外看，就可以看到漂亮的风景。
text.pinyin: Cóng wǒ fángjiān de chuānghu wǎng wài kàn, jiù kěyǐ kàndào piàoliang de fēngjǐng.
text.english: Looking outside from my room’s window, you can see beautiful scenery.

examples.teachingNote: A visible landmark gives the direction.

text.traditional: 從這裡往最高的那棟房子走，你會看到兩家百貨公司。
text.simplified: 从这里往最高的那栋房子走，你会看到两家百货公司。
text.pinyin: Cóng zhèlǐ wǎng zuì gāo de nà dòng fángzi zǒu, nǐ huì kàndào liǎng jiā bǎihuò gōngsī.
text.english: Walk from here toward the tallest building, and you will see two department stores.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: Get on the Internet with a Cell Phone
grammarPages.titleEnglish: Read the Time and Result Meanings of 就
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Recognize something early or a result that follows.
grammarPages.explanation: In a time scene, 就 can mean earlier than expected. After an instruction or condition, 就 can introduce the result. 就 can also show that something is easy to complete or likely to happen — 往前走，就可以看到那家店了。

lessonWorld.title: Get to the museum before it opens
lessonWorld.prompt: The route is short: walk five minutes and you arrive.
lessonWorld.traditional: 往右走，五分鐘就到了。
lessonWorld.simplified: 往右走，五分钟就到了。
lessonWorld.pinyin: Wǎng yòu zǒu, wǔ fēnzhōng jiù dào le.
lessonWorld.english: Walk right and you will arrive in five minutes.

grammarPages.pattern: Time + 就 + action / Instruction， 就 + result

subject.traditional: 九點開始上班，可是我每天都
subject.simplified: 九点开始上班，可是我每天都
subject.pinyin: jiǔ diǎn kāishǐ shàngbān, kěshì wǒ měitiān dōu
subject.meaning: work starts at nine, but I every day

patternRows.english: Work starts at nine, but I arrive at the company at eight thirty every day.
Walk ahead, then arrive.
Take a look first, then know.

items.question: He got to work at 8:30, before 9:00. 就 or 才?
items.answer: 就 — “as early as 8:30,” good news. 才 would say “not until 8:30,” which sounds too late.

right.pinyin: Tā bā diǎn bàn jiù dào le.
right.english: He arrived as early as 8:30.

items.question: Where does 就 sit in a result sentence?
items.answer: Right before the result action: 就 + action. Never after it.

right.english: Take a look first, then you will know.

items.question: I woke up at six. Do I need 了 at the end?
items.answer: Yes. An early finished moment uses the pair 就 + action + 了.

right.pinyin: Wǒ liù diǎn jiù qǐchuáng le.
right.english: I got up as early as six.

discoveryLab.title: Two scenes, two jobs for 就
discoveryLab.description: Do not force one English translation. Let the scene reveal the job.

choices.label: Earlier than expected
choices.traditional: 九點上班，我八點半就到了。
choices.simplified: 九点上班，我八点半就到了。
choices.pinyin: Jiǔ diǎn shàngbān, wǒ bā diǎn bàn jiù dào le.
choices.english: Work starts at nine; I arrived as early as 8:30.
choices.note: The expected time is nine. 就 highlights the early arrival.

choices.label: Then you see it
choices.traditional: 往前走，就可以看到博物館。
choices.simplified: 往前走，就可以看到博物馆。
choices.pinyin: Wǎng qián zǒu, jiù kěyǐ kàndào bówùguǎn.
choices.english: Walk forward, then you can see the museum.
choices.note: The first action produces the result after 就.

choices.label: Then it is fine
choices.traditional: 先跟老師請假，就沒問題了。
choices.simplified: 先跟老师请假，就没问题了。
choices.pinyin: Xiān gēn lǎoshī qǐngjià, jiù méi wèntí le.
choices.english: Ask the teacher for leave first; then there is no problem.
choices.note: 就 introduces the result of the solution.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Time scene: sooner than expected. Action scene: then this result follows.

examples.teachingNote: Earlier than expected.

text.traditional: 九點開始上班，可是我每天都八點半就到公司了。
text.simplified: 九点开始上班，可是我每天都八点半就到公司了。
text.pinyin: Jiǔ diǎn kāishǐ shàngbān, kěshì wǒ měitiān dōu bā diǎn bàn jiù dào gōngsī le.
text.english: Work starts at nine, but I arrive at the office by 8:30 every day.

examples.teachingNote: The time is surprisingly early.

text.traditional: 我今天早上六點就起床了。
text.simplified: 我今天早上六点就起床了。
text.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān zǎoshang liù diǎn jiù qǐchuáng le.
text.english: I got up as early as six this morning.

examples.teachingNote: An instruction produces a result.

text.traditional: 你往前走，就可以看到那家店了。
text.simplified: 你往前走，就可以看到那家店了。
text.pinyin: Nǐ wǎng qián zǒu, jiù kěyǐ kàndào nà jiā diàn le.
text.english: Walk forward, then you can see the shop.

examples.teachingNote: A solution produces a result.

text.traditional: 你先跟老師請假，就沒問題了吧？
text.simplified: 你先跟老师请假，就没问题了吧？
text.pinyin: Nǐ xiān gēn lǎoshī qǐngjià, jiù méi wèntí le ba?
text.english: Ask the teacher for leave first; then there is no problem.

questions.correctFeedback: 就 highlights the earlier-than-expected arrival.

dialogue.title: 對話一 · Dialogue 1
dialogue.setting: 國安給中明打電話 · Guoan calls Zhongming

text.traditional: 喂，中明，半個小時以前我寄了一封電子郵件給你，你看到了嗎？
text.simplified: 喂，中明，半个小时以前我寄了一封电子邮件给你，你看到了吗？
text.pinyin: Wèi, Zhōngmíng, bàn ge xiǎoshí yǐqián wǒ jì le yì fēng diànzǐ yóujiàn gěi nǐ, nǐ kàndào le ma?
text.english: Hello, Zhongming, I sent you an email half an hour ago. Have you read it?

text.traditional: 剛剛我的手機網路有點兒問題，不能看電子郵件，你寄的是什麼？
text.simplified: 刚刚我的手机网路有点儿问题，不能看电子邮件，你寄的是什么？
text.pinyin: Gānggāng wǒ de shǒujī wǎnglù yǒudiǎnr wèntí, bù néng kàn diànzǐ yóujiàn, nǐ jì de shì shénme?
text.english: The internet connection on my phone just had a little problem; I couldn’t read your email. What did you send me?

text.traditional: 博物館的網址。下禮拜六老師要帶我們去參觀，你可以先看看。
text.simplified: 博物馆的网址。下礼拜六老师要带我们去参观，你可以先看看。
text.pinyin: Bówùguǎn de wǎngzhǐ. Xià lǐbàiliù lǎoshī yào dài wǒmen qù cānguān, nǐ kěyǐ xiān kànkan.
text.english: I sent you a link for the museum website. The teacher is taking us to visit there next Saturday; you can take a look first.

text.traditional: 好。（看看手機）現在沒問題了，我看到了。
text.simplified: 好。（看看手机）现在没问题了，我看到了。
text.pinyin: Hǎo. (Kànkan shǒujī) Xiànzài méi wèntí le, wǒ kàndào le.
text.english: OK. (Take a look at the phone) There’s no problem now, I’ve read your email.

text.traditional: 網站上有地址，那個地方在我家附近，從我家出去，往右轉，差不多五分鐘就到了。
text.simplified: 网站上有地址，那个地方在我家附近，从我家出去，往右转，差不多五分钟就到了。
text.pinyin: Wǎngzhàn shang yǒu dìzhǐ, nà ge dìfang zài wǒ jiā fùjìn, cóng wǒ jiā chūqù, wǎng yòu zhuǎn, chàbuduō wǔ fēnzhōng jiù dào le.
text.english: There’s the address on the website; that place is close to my house. If you go from my place, you make a right turn, and you’ll be there in just about five minutes.

text.traditional: 我們應該幾點到？
text.simplified: 我们应该几点到？
text.pinyin: Wǒmen yīnggāi jǐ diǎn dào?
text.english: What time should we be there?

text.traditional: 早上九點在博物館門口見，要記得準時到。
text.simplified: 早上九点在博物馆门口见，要记得准时到。
text.pinyin: Zǎoshang jiǔ diǎn zài bówùguǎn ménkǒu jiàn, yào jìde zhǔnshí dào.
text.english: 9 a.m. at the museum gate. Remember to get there on time.

text.traditional: 我們上個星期六去運動的時候，我到得太晚，真不好意思。下個星期我一定會準時。
text.simplified: 我们上个星期六去运动的时候，我到得太晚，真不好意思。下个星期我一定会准时。
text.pinyin: Wǒmen shàng ge xīngqīliù qù yùndòng de shíhòu, wǒ dào de tài wǎn, zhēn bù hǎoyìsi. Xià ge xīngqī wǒ yídìng huì zhǔnshí.
text.english: I am sorry for being late when we went exercising last Saturday. I’ll definitely be on time next week.

comprehension.hint: Listen for the duration before 就到了.

items.title: Grammar 4–5 · Countdown and duration

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: Get on the Internet with a Cell Phone
grammarPages.titleEnglish: Start a Countdown with 就要…了
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say that an event is about to happen.
grammarPages.explanation: 就要 or 快要 places an event very near. Sentence-final 了 signals that the new situation is arriving.

lessonWorld.title: Get to the museum before it opens
lessonWorld.prompt: It is 8:55. The museum opens at nine.
lessonWorld.traditional: 博物館五分鐘以後就要開門了。
lessonWorld.simplified: 博物馆五分钟以后就要开门了。
lessonWorld.pinyin: Bówùguǎn wǔ fēnzhōng yǐhòu jiù yào kāimén le.
lessonWorld.english: The museum will open in five minutes.

grammarPages.pattern: Time clue + 就要／快要 + event + 了

patternRows.english: The doors will open in five minutes.
They are returning home tomorrow.
It is about to begin.

items.question: The film is about to start. Do I need 了 at the end?
items.answer: Yes. 就要／快要 + event + 了 keeps 了 at the very end: 電影馬上就要開始了。 With a time word like 馬上, 電影馬上就開始了。 is also fine.

right.pinyin: Diànyǐng mǎshàng jiù yào kāishǐ le.
right.english: The film is about to start.

items.question: He is about to go back home. Is 他回國就要了 right?
items.answer: No. Put 就要 before the event and 了 at the very end: 就要 + event + 了.

right.english: He is about to go back to his home country.

items.question: Zhongming is almost here. Where does 快要 go?
items.answer: Before the event: 快要 + event + 了. Never after it.

right.english: Zhongming is almost here.

discoveryLab.title: Match the countdown clock
discoveryLab.description: Choose the sentence whose event is close to the current moment.

choices.label: Doors open
choices.pinyin: Bówùguǎn jiù yào kāimén le.
choices.english: The museum is about to open.
choices.note: The closed doors and near opening time create the countdown.

choices.label: Movie starts
choices.pinyin: Diànyǐng mǎshàng jiù yào kāishǐ le.
choices.english: The movie is about to start.
choices.note: 馬上 strengthens the sense of “very soon.”

choices.label: Almost here
choices.pinyin: Zhōngmíng kuài yào dào le.
choices.english: Zhongming is almost here.
choices.note: 快要 works without 就 in this source pattern.

choices.label: Next month
choices.pinyin: Wǒ xià ge yuè jiù yào huíguó le.
choices.english: I will return home next month.
choices.note: A known approaching change can use the countdown frame.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Look for an approaching change: 就要／快要 + event + 了.

examples.teachingNote: An approaching future change.

text.traditional: 我下個月就要回國了。
text.simplified: 我下个月就要回国了。
text.pinyin: Wǒ xià ge yuè jiù yào huíguó le.
text.english: I will return home next month.

examples.teachingNote: A near arrival.

text.traditional: 他的女朋友明天就要來了，他非常開心。
text.simplified: 他的女朋友明天就要来了，他非常开心。
text.pinyin: Tā de nǚpéngyǒu míngtiān jiù yào lái le, tā fēicháng kāixīn.
text.english: His girlfriend is coming tomorrow; he is very happy.

examples.teachingNote: The source also allows 就 + event + 了 without 要.

text.traditional: 電影馬上就開始了，他怎麼還沒來？
text.simplified: 电影马上就开始了，他怎么还没来？
text.pinyin: Diànyǐng mǎshàng jiù kāishǐ le, tā zěnme hái méi lái?
text.english: The movie is about to start; why is he not here yet?

examples.teachingNote: A closing countdown.

text.traditional: 圖書館就要關了，你現在去也許太晚了。
text.simplified: 图书馆就要关了，你现在去也许太晚了。
text.pinyin: Túshūguǎn jiù yào guān le, nǐ xiànzài qù yěxǔ tài wǎn le.
text.english: The library is about to close; if you go now, it may be too late.

grammarPages.exercisePreview: Choose the event that is approaching now.
grammarPages.exerciseInstruction: Complete each about-to-happen sentence.

segments.hint: Use 就要 + event + 了.

questions.correctFeedback: The countdown signal comes before the event.
questions.repairFeedback: Use 就要 + event + 了.

segments.hint: Build 就要 + action + 了.

questions.correctFeedback: 馬上 and 就要 both point forward to 開始.
questions.repairFeedback: Build 就要 + action + 了.

segments.hint: Use 快要 + event + 了.

questions.correctFeedback: 快要 comes before the approaching arrival.
questions.repairFeedback: Use 快要 + event + 了.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: Get on the Internet with a Cell Phone
grammarPages.titleTraditional: 量出一個動作做了多久
grammarPages.titleEnglish: Measure an Action’s Duration
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say how long an action lasts.
grammarPages.explanation: Duration follows the action. With some activities that pair an action word with a thing, Chinese repeats the action word or uses duration + 的 before the thing.

lessonWorld.title: Measure the whole journey
lessonWorld.prompt: The group waits ten minutes and visits for three hours.
lessonWorld.traditional: 我們排隊排十分鐘，參觀三個小時。
lessonWorld.simplified: 我们排队排十分钟，参观三个小时。
lessonWorld.pinyin: Wǒmen páiduì pái shí fēnzhōng, cānguān sān ge xiǎoshí.
lessonWorld.english: We wait in line for ten minutes and visit for three hours.

grammarPages.pattern: Action + duration / Activity + action + duration

patternRows.english: Work for eight hours.
I run for thirty minutes every day.
I sleep for seven hours every day.
Attend class for three hours.
I sleep seven hours every day.

items.question: I slept three hours. Can I say 我睡覺三個小時?
items.answer: No. A two-part action word needs its first part again: 睡了三個小時的覺 (or 睡覺睡三個小時).

right.pinyin: Wǒ shuì le sān ge xiǎoshí de jiào.
right.english: I slept for three hours.

items.question: Why does 睡 repeat AFTER 睡覺, not inside it?
items.answer: For duration, repeat the first action word after the whole word: 睡覺睡十分鐘. 睡睡覺 would mean “sleep a bit” — not a count of time.

right.english: I sleep for ten minutes.

items.question: I study Chinese for three hours. Where does the time go?
items.answer: With a thing after the action, use duration + 的 + thing: 學三個小時的中文.

right.pinyin: Wǒ xué sān ge xiǎoshí de Zhōngwén.
right.english: I study Chinese for three hours.

discoveryLab.title: Attach the clock to the action
discoveryLab.description: Start with the simplest shape, then watch what happens when the activity also names a thing.

choices.label: Work
choices.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān gōngzuò bā ge xiǎoshí.
choices.english: I work eight hours every day.
choices.note: A simple action can take duration directly.

choices.label: Sleep
choices.traditional: 我每天睡覺睡七個小時。
choices.simplified: 我每天睡觉睡七个小时。
choices.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān shuìjiào shuì qī ge xiǎoshí.
choices.english: I sleep seven hours every day.
choices.note: The action word from 睡覺 repeats before the duration.

choices.label: Class
choices.traditional: 我明天要上課上三個小時。
choices.simplified: 我明天要上课上三个小时。
choices.pinyin: Wǒ míngtiān yào shàngkè shàng sān ge xiǎoshí.
choices.english: I will attend class for three hours tomorrow.
choices.note: 上 repeats after the two-part activity 上課.

choices.label: Study Chinese
choices.traditional: 我每天學三個小時的中文。
choices.simplified: 我每天学三个小时的中文。
choices.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān xué sān ge xiǎoshí de Zhōngwén.
choices.english: I study Chinese for three hours every day.
choices.note: Duration + 的 can sit before the thing you study, 中文.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Keep the duration attached to the action—not floating at the end of the whole story.

examples.teachingNote: Simple action + duration.

text.traditional: 我每天工作八個小時。
text.simplified: 我每天工作八个小时。
text.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān gōngzuò bā ge xiǎoshí.
text.english: I work eight hours every day.

examples.teachingNote: Duration follows the action.

text.traditional: 爸爸每天早上運動三十分鐘。
text.simplified: 爸爸每天早上运动三十分钟。
text.pinyin: Bàba měitiān zǎoshang yùndòng sānshí fēnzhōng.
text.english: Dad exercises thirty minutes every morning.

examples.teachingNote: Repeat the verb from the activity.

text.traditional: 我每天跑步跑三十分鐘。
text.simplified: 我每天跑步跑三十分钟。
text.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān pǎobù pǎo sānshí fēnzhōng.
text.english: I run for thirty minutes every day.

examples.teachingNote: Duration + 的 appears before the thing.

text.traditional: 我明天要開六個小時的車，我想先去睡覺。
text.simplified: 我明天要开六个小时的车，我想先去睡觉。
text.pinyin: Wǒ míngtiān yào kāi liù ge xiǎoshí de chē, wǒ xiǎng xiān qù shuìjiào.
text.english: I have to drive six hours tomorrow; I want to go to sleep first.

text.traditional: 我們從學校走十分鐘，就可以到那家銀行了。
text.simplified: 我们从学校走十分钟，就可以到那家银行了。
text.pinyin: Wǒmen cóng xuéxiào zǒu shí fēnzhōng, jiù kěyǐ dào nà jiā yínháng le.
text.english: If we walk ten minutes from school, we can get to that bank.

text.traditional: 今天我們打算參觀三個小時，會有人給我們介紹。進去以後，記得要安靜，不可以說話說得太大聲。
text.simplified: 今天我们打算参观三个小时，会有人给我们介绍。进去以后，记得要安静，不可以说话说得太大声。
text.pinyin: Jīntiān wǒmen dǎsuàn cānguān sān ge xiǎoshí, huì yǒu rén gěi wǒmen jièshào. Jìnqù yǐhòu, jìde yào ānjìng, bù kěyǐ shuōhuà shuō de tài dàshēng.

text.traditional: 老師，我剛剛先用手機上網看了很多有趣的圖片，真想馬上就看到博物館裡的東西。
text.simplified: 老师，我刚刚先用手机上网看了很多有趣的图片，真想马上就看到博物馆里的东西。
text.pinyin: Lǎoshī, wǒ gānggāng xiān yòng shǒujī shàngwǎng kàn le hěn duō yǒuqù de túpiàn, zhēn xiǎng mǎshàng jiù kàndào bówùguǎn lǐ de dōngxi.
text.english: Teacher, I just used my cell phone to look for some information on the internet, and I saw many interesting pictures. I want to see what they have in the museum right away.

text.traditional: 我知道你非常喜歡歷史，我想你今天一定會很開心。
text.simplified: 我知道你非常喜欢历史，我想你今天一定会很开心。
text.pinyin: Wǒ zhīdào nǐ fēicháng xǐhuān lìshǐ, wǒ xiǎng nǐ jīntiān yídìng huì hěn kāixīn.
